per_object_cap.stated: Sizes: 'small 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 12 GB' at USD 0.018 an hour, 'default 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 50 GB' at USD 0.036, 'large 8 vCPU / 16 GB / 125 GB' at USD 0.072, 'xlarge 16 vCPU / 32 GB / 251 GB' at USD 0.200, the last needing the USD 100 plan.
per_object_cap.notes: Every size is a full Linux virtual machine with a public IPv6 address and public URLs for its ports.

interface_detail: HTTP API at https://boat.dev/api/v1 plus a CLI; hostPort exposes a port on a public URL
tooling: boat CLI, Python SDK, REST; GET /limits reports the balance in seconds of default time
chaining: the only cheap sandbox here that publishes a public URL per port and an IPv6 address per sandbox
limits_note: Included plan time expires at the end of the month; credit packs cost USD 20 and never expire, which is the only way to bank time.
reliability_note: A stopped box loses its disk after 14 days, which is shorter than most providers here and is stated in a warning block rather than a footnote.

free_tier.stated: No signup credit. 'Your first plan starts with a 7-day free trial. A card is required. The trial has its own lower limits.' A plan is prepaid time: 'boat grants the included time each month. It expires at the end of the month.'
free_tier.notes: A plan credit, not a grant: USD 20 buys 555 hours of the default size and the balance lapses monthly.

retention.stated: A stopped sandbox keeps its disk for 14 days, then 'boat deletes the data, and the sandbox cannot resume'. Saved snapshots have no auto-deletion date.

egress.terms: 'Network traffic. boat does not bill egress.'
